content: I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!

Looks like a fun puzzle! Rules * Optional: consider adding "to" between "move" and "or shoot into" (noting that "to" is used after "move" in the Output section). * Please specify whether two or more features (bats, a shaft, the Mumpus) can occupy the same room. * Please specify whether bats and the Mumpus always remains in their initial rooms or can move during the game. Expert rules * "After transporting you, the bat flies away, leaving the original room unoccupied": what exactly happens to the bat afterwards? • Does it leave the cave entirely? • Does it move to another room? • If so, does it choose an unexplored room or any room at random? • Can it move into a room that already contains a hazard? • If it prefers unexplored safe rooms, what happens when none remain? My assumption is that the bat simply leaves the cave, but it'd be helpful to state this explicitly. * Optional: consider adding "to" between "move" and "or shoot into" here as well. Input * Please add "space-separated" after each of the three occurrences of "Three". Input for a game round * Please add line numbers, for example: Line 1: One integer (etc.) Similarly for Lines 2 and 3. * Please add "the room IDs of" before "the three adjacent rooms". * For the clue inputs, please add ", 0 otherwise" to each description. Output * Please change "One command" to "One of the following commands". * Please format "MOVE" and "SHOOT" using the tag instead of . * Please format "roomId" using the tag instead of . Constraints * Please format all variable names using the tag. * Optional: it'd be helpful to specify the range of valid room IDs (0 to roomCount - 1?). * Please specify that the starting room is always safe and free of bats. * If solvability is guaranteed, please state that every case can be solved without guessing. Stub generator * Interesting; I didn't know it was possible to include a variable directly in a write statement. How did you write that? Cases, viewer and error messages * I'll review these once the above points have been addressed. Thanks.

OK. I believe I have addressed those comments and added a few other clarifications.
Here is my stub:
```
read roomCount:int batCount:int shaftCount:int

gameloop
read currentRoom:int
read roomA:int roomB:int roomC:int
read bats:int shaft:int mumpus:int

write join("MOVE", roomA)

OUTPUT
MOVE roomId | SHOOT roomId
```

Thanks for the stub generator code. I wasn't aware that defined variables could be used directly in a write statement.

Also, thank you for updating the statement. The revision has resolved most ambiguities.

Rules
* Please apply the bullet-point format to the items that aren't currently formatted so.

* The final sentence appears to imply that some cases may be random and could require guessing. Could you clarify?

* I assume no guessing should be needed. If so, consider removing "non-random" and adding "are non-random and" after "validators".

Expert Rules
* Point 1: Please remove "preferably one" and add "if any exists" at the end.

* Please change "caves" to "cave" (twice).

* Optional: consider adding "to" between "move" and "or shoot into" here (noting that "to" is used after "move" in the Output section).

* Consider mentioning the option to toggle room numbers in the viewer.

Input
* Please change "your current room number" to "the room ID of your current room" for consistency.

Output
* Please use line breaks in a consistent style in the descriptions of MOVE and SHOOT.

Constraints
* Please remove the final two constraints (they'll be moved to a new "Defeat conditions" section, see below).

* Please format all variable names using the <var> tag.

* Please add (with <var> tags):
batsCount + shaftsCount + 5 < roomCount

  (The 5 accounts for the Mumpus room, the starting room, and the three rooms adjacent to the starting room.)

* Please add (with <var> tags):
0 <= roomId < roomCount

  (Sorry for the confusion by describing this as optional in my previous comment).

* Please state that all <var>roomId</var>s are distinct.

Input / Constraints / Stub generator
* Please standardise variable names:
  • batsCount vs batCount
  • shaftsCount vs shaftCount
  • a vs roomA
  • b vs roomB
  • c vs roomC

Victory / Defeat conditions
* Please insert these two sections before the Expert Rules. The source code of this page includes an example of the HTML code to use: https://www.codingame.com/ide/puzzle/flames-extinguisher

Cases
* The shuffled-room-number cases (Tiny Validator, Medium Validator, Dodecahedron - Classic, and Tiny Hard Validator) don't provide adjacent room IDs in ascending order.

* Are these the only cases that use shuffled room numbers? If so, may I suggest adding more such cases in both fixed and random tests and validators?

* Could the cases include a greater variety of hazard counts? Currently, the bat count is usually 1 or 2 (except for two tests with 10 bats), while the shaft count is always between 0 and 3. There are cases with no shafts, but none with no bats.

* What are the main differences between the "Classic - Random Bats" and "Classic - Crazy Bats" tests?

* If there are no major differences, please convert one of the tests into a validator, as no validator covers the scenario with 10 bats.

Referee
* Outputting "MOVE 9" or "MOVE -1" (or SHOOT instead of MOVE) causes Test 1 to crash (out-of-bounds error).

Thanks.

I'm not sure whether you've finished updating the puzzle, but below is the current list of outstanding items:

Rules
* Please fix the bullet-point formatting in the fifth-last point.

Expert Rules
* In the first bullet point, please remove "preferably one" and add "if any exists" at the end.

* Consider mentioning the option to toggle room numbers in the viewer.

* Consider moving the final part ("Each turn, you must decide … you only have one arrow.") to the Goal section. It seems more natural to tell players upfront that they only have one arrow, before later explaining that shooting it into the wrong room results in defeat.

Loss Conditions
* "Unrecognized command" and "Attempt to act on non-adjacent room" are two distinct loss conditions. Please split them into separate bullet points.

* Please add "Timeout" as a loss condition.

Input
* Please change "roomId" to "room ID".

Output
* Please use line breaks in a consistent style in the descriptions of MOVE and SHOOT. For example, you could add a line break after "into an adjacent room.".

Constraints
* In the final constraint, please change the second "<=" to "<".

* Please add (with <var> tags):
batsCount + shaftsCount + 5 < roomCount

  (The 5 accounts for the Mumpus room, the starting room, and the three rooms adjacent to the starting room.)

Input / Constraints / Stub
* Please standardise the variable names:
  • batsCount vs batCount
  • shaftsCount vs shaftCount

Cases
* Could the cases include a greater variety of hazard counts? Currently, the bat count is usually 1 or 2 (except for two tests with 10 bats), while the shaft count is always between 0 and 3. There are cases with no shafts, but none with no bats.

* What are the main differences between the "Classic - Random Bats" and "Classic - Crazy Bats" tests?

* If there are no major differences, please convert one of the tests into a validator, as no validator covers the scenario with 10 bats.

Thanks.

I fixed a few things but I'm still working on it.
I plan to redo some of the levels, add some more, and rename them.

I believe I've addressed these concerns. Let me know if I missed anything.
I did not add the line about the number of bats being less than the number of rooms. I think that's pretty obvious.
I did not add anything about timeouts since I didn't do anything special with the time limits; I'm just using the defaults.

Added and removed levels and gave them more consistent names.
I think we're getting pretty close final draft.
